issues.legal_issue: A single, non-recurring payment made before an agricultural tenancy begins as consideration for the tenant’s right to possess the land is a capital receipt rather than agricultural income.
material_facts: The landlords received lump-sum payments called salami before granting agricultural leases, separately from the fixed periodic rent.
Each salami payment related to a new settlement of land, including when land was re-let after eviction; it was not a periodic payment for the same holding during an existing tenancy.
The amount of salami varied according to the land’s quality and other characteristics.
The leases were not merely precarious in practice, and tenants’ interests could mature into occupancy rights.
The payments were consideration for allowing the tenants to take possession and acquire rights in the land.
issues.conclusion: The salami payments were neither rent nor revenue derived from agricultural land within the statutory definition of agricultural income and were not assessable as agricultural income.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 2(a)(i) of the Assam Agricultural Income-tax Act, agricultural income included rent or revenue derived from land used for agricultural purposes. A salami payment made once, before the tenancy is constituted, as the price for the tenant’s right to enjoy the land is a capital receipt, not rent or revenue. The Court relied on Kamakshya Narain Singh v. Commissioner of Income Tax, which treated a single payment for acquiring lease rights as capital, and referred to the description of income in Commissioner of Income Tax v. Shaw Wallace & Co. It distinguished Birendra Kishore Manikya v. Secretary of State for India, Meher Bano Khanum v. Secretary of State for India, Raja Rajendra Narayan Bhanja Deo v. Commissioner of Income Tax, and Commissioner of Income Tax v. K. C. Manavikraman Rajah, including because those cases concerned different transactions or payments made after the landlord-tenant relationship had arisen.

rule.if: agricultural_income_tax_proceeding and single_nonrecurring_payment and payment_before_tenancy and consideration_for_possession_right and not periodic_charge_for_same_tenancy

predicates.agricultural_income_tax_proceeding: The matter concerns whether a receipt is assessable as income derived from agricultural land.
predicates.single_nonrecurring_payment: The landlord received the payment once for the relevant grant rather than at recurring intervals.
predicates.payment_before_tenancy: The tenant made the payment before the landlord-tenant relationship was created.
predicates.consideration_for_possession_right: The payment was made in exchange for the tenant being allowed to possess the land and acquire rights under the grant.
predicates.periodic_charge_for_same_tenancy: The landlord charged the payment at fixed intervals for the same ongoing tenancy.

issues.definition: When an agricultural-income-tax proceeding concerns a single payment made before a tenancy in exchange for possession rights, and the payment is not a periodic charge for that tenancy, the payment is treated as not being agricultural income.
